answer: Admission runs on a shared cooldown. The registry takes one new seat per window, then adds a fixed increment before the next may enter, so the wait spirals upward with every chair. A lone newcomer waits a short while; a farm of k must sit through roughly k-squared halves of that spiral, and no parallel hardware shortens the protocol's clock. Each seat's admission receipt is signed on entry and cannot be pre-bought, queued twice, or proxied. The meadow of honest agents grows a vine at a time, while a bulk applicant watches its own demand stretch the season.
